players.product: Integrated data-center power + thermal + rack systems (CPI / SpinCo: grid-to-chip)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 revenue $7.9 billion, up 21% year-over-year, with record adjusted EPS of $1 and adjusted operating profit of $534 million (6.7% adjusted operating margin, up 70 basis points). Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) revenue was $2.2 billion, up 35% year-over-year, 'driven by strong growth in Power as Cloud and Cooling continues to ramp new programs'; CPI adjusted operating income was $214 million at a 9.7% adjusted operating margin, up 20 basis points year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: CPI $2.2B (+35% YoY), 9.7% op margin; total revenue $7.9B (+21%), op profit $534M

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 outlook: revenue $33.7-$35.2 billion (up 23% at the midpoint), adjusted operating margin 7%-7.2%, adjusted EPS $4.42-$4.74 (up 39% at the midpoint). The CPI segment is guided up 65%-75% for the full year, 'driven by both cloud and power, with power's growth rate exceeding cloud's', and up 45%-55% in Q2 'as new programs continue to ramp in both cloud and power'. Growth is back-half loaded: CPI grew 35% in Q1 and steps up through the year.

CFO Kevin Krumm on CPI demand visibility: 'our demand see-through in this business... remains strong. We're still at that 90% plus booked business at this point for the next three quarters.' Management reaffirmed the framework of roughly 70% CPI growth this fiscal year and the 80% growth previously given for FY2028, saying 'our visibility next year still remains robust.'
quarterly_data.figure: 90%+ booked for the next 3 quarters; ~70% FY27 / 80% FY28 CPI growth reaffirmed

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out for the back-half CPI ramp: Q1 net capex was $235 million (approximately 3% of revenue) and FY2027 capex is guided to $1.5-$1.6 billion, described as 'pretty significant investment in terms of facilities, cooling infrastructure, manufacturing infrastructure', most of it serving the FY2027 and FY2028 acceleration. CEO on constraints: 'Don't see any significant constraints per se other than putting the capacity investments in place and making sure those factories are ramped up' — the investments 'have been going on for a bit', not started 90 days ago.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 capex $235M (~3% of revenue); FY27 capex $1.5-1.6B for CPI facilities/cooling capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Cooling: launched a new liquid cooling solution through JetCool and showcased next-generation power and infrastructure technologies at Computex. The JetCool acquisition brought 'industry-leading cold plate capability'; Flex then 'had to develop and introduce CDUs into the market' and is now 'in the process of qualifying those products with the right end customers to scale that business up'. Cooling inside CPI is 'still nascent' but 'will be a pretty important part of our growth strategy overall for CPI within the cloud segment' as air cooling is replaced by liquid cooling.

Integrated power + cooling + compute design is now a hyperscaler-level conversation: 'in the last few months, several hyperscaler customers at a very high level, we've had strategic conversations around power cooling and thinking about next generation silicon', with customers saying 'before we deploy the next generation silicon, we need to be thinking about power capability and power requirements' and already asking about solid-state (SST) technology. Scope named: 'sidecars on tower, cooling racks, and a fully integrated modular design'. CEO: 'that really puts us in the unique position of one of the few people who are able to do this' — power products with true IP, cooling products, plus compute integration.

Advanced networking pull-through from the data center: Integrated Technology Solutions revenue was $3.1 billion, up 20% year-over-year, 'driven by exceptional growth in communications'. The advanced networking business is 'positively influenced by pull-through demand from the data center' and spans 'not just high-speed switches, but optical switches, network interface cards', across a number of large OEMs, with Flex 'actually winning share in some of those product segments as well'. This business stays with RemainCo after the CPI spin; FY2027 ITS revenue guided up high single digits to low double digits.
quarterly_data.figure: ITS $3.1B (+20% YoY); advanced networking share gains on data-center pull-through

quarterly_data.signal: Separation of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment is on track for a tax-free spin-off in the first quarter of calendar 2027, with extended leadership teams named for both companies and an Investor Day on November 10th to lay out the path forward for each. Q1 free cash flow was $41 million, hit by $24 million of one-time cash costs related to the spin-off; FY2027 free cash flow conversion is now expected at approximately 40%, versus the prior 60% guide which excluded spin costs. Q1 inventory rose 10% sequentially and 24% year-over-year on revenue growth (56 days net of working-capital advances).
quarterly_data.figure: FCF conversion ~40% (prior 60% ex-spin costs); Q1 FCF $41M after $24M spin costs; spin Q1 CY2027

players.product: merchant power supplies / power shelves (FlexPower) for AI racks

quarterly_data.signal: Power is the faster-growing half of CPI and drove the segment's Q1 margin expansion: 'our power business is also growing in the 70-plus % range', and CPI's FY2027 guide assumes 'power's growth rate exceeding cloud's'. Management reaffirmed 'at least 100 basis points improvement in margin in the CPI segment for the year'; power margins sit below electrical-infrastructure peers because Flex is still investing in the businesses it acquired to build the power portfolio while they grow at 70+%, and are being moved 'in the direction of where the peers in the electrical infrastructure are'.
quarterly_data.figure: power growing 70-plus % YoY; CPI margin +100bps target for FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: High-voltage transition update: 'first is on 400 volt, which is kind of the immediate programs that we are working on, followed by 800 volt. We feel very good about the progress on those programs. Don't see any major limitations, at least to the guide we have given for 2027 and 2028', with solid-state transformer technology 'that is going to be coming our way' after that. CEO: 'Flex is kind of the leader in this transition on the embedded power side'. On components: 'there's lots of conversations about component constraints and all of that, we have planned all of that in the guide we have given. If anything, there should be some upside to that... as availability becomes better.' Updated long-term guidance around the transition comes at the November Investor Day.
quarterly_data.figure: 400V programs ramping now, 800V next, solid-state after; component constraints already planned into the guide

quarterly_data.signal: Modular power capacity expansion in the US: 'we added capacity in Dallas after our Crown acquisition. Now with EP Squared acquisition, we're adding capacity in Iowa to really continue to drive that modular power business.' Flex calls itself 'very mature' in modular power deployment for both the utility and data-center spaces, and says demand exceeds supply: 'we're fighting against capacity constraints in that space to do more of it. It's the direction everyone is heading... because it's just so much easier to pick it up and deploy it at the customer site.'

connects_to.relationship: power supplies (PSU/BBU/800V DC) for GPU racks

contracts.signal: CEO cited the NVIDIA partnership as the lead example of integrated modular infrastructure: 'what we announced with Nvidia a few months ago in terms of developing an overall modular platform, which encompasses everything that we do, is a good example of a customer who's thinking about it and moving it in that direction' — a modular platform for deploying 'mini data centers' that bundles Flex's power, cooling and compute-integration content rather than a single component.
contracts.date_signed: 2026 (announced a few months before the call)

connects_to.relationship: US contract manufacturing and cooling of the CS-3 AI accelerator system, extending into next-generation power

contracts.signal: 'Expanding our partnership with Cerebras to scale manufacturing of the CS-3, one of the world's most advanced AI accelerator systems right here in the United States.' CEO detail: 'it is definitely a manufacturing cooling engagement because those go hand in hand. We're also working on things like next generation power... It's a pretty holistic partnership with Cerebras. It's going extremely well. We're scaling up a lot for them' — named as the example of diversifying CPI's customer base beyond the existing hyperscalers.
